reason: The heated extraction head is a plausible way to draw water from the surveyed ice bore.
expectation: The head should establish a way to melt and extract water from the ice.

effect: The extraction head established a sealed well producing cloudy water, so the next step is to connect it to treatment.
reaction: The closed melt pocket is a satisfying, physically clear start.
reason: The clean service hose should connect the melt well to the water processor.
expectation: The hose will connect to the well, preparing a route for water to reach treatment.

effect: The well is connected to the processor, with grit collecting at the raw-water strainer; treatment still needs to be completed.
reaction: The strainer makes the treatment line feel physically grounded.
reason: The connected line and water processor are the most direct pairing for bringing the water through treatment.
expectation: The processor will treat the water from the connected well line.

effect: The processor produced checked drinking water, and the new goal is to protect the exterior run.
reaction: The treatment sequence was clear and satisfying.
reason: Insulation felt plausibly protects the exterior water line from the cold.
expectation: The felt will insulate the exterior run, perhaps as part of a protective covering.

effect: The felt cannot be applied directly to the well line; its listed partner is packing foil.
reaction: The compatibility hint clarifies the next step.
reason: The felt and foil are the available compatible pair and plausibly make a protective wrap.
expectation: They will form an insulated covering for the exterior run.

effect: The felt and foil formed a flexible insulation jacket for the hose.
reaction: The overlapping seam makes the construction clear.
reason: The jacket is designed to protect the exterior hose run.
expectation: The jacket will wrap and protect the exterior water line.

effect: The jacket protected the heat-traced hose and completed the chapter; insulation slows heat loss while the tracing supplies heat.
reaction: The distinction between insulation and active heating was a useful, satisfying detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the water line through extraction, straining and treatment was the most worthwhile passage: each connection had a clear purpose and the result explained how the water became usable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to apply the felt directly to the line was the least worthwhile step; the compatibility feedback was useful, but it added a small detour.

surprise.text: The final explanation clarified that insulation only slows heat loss and that the hose's tracing still supplies heat.

arbitrary.text: The need to join foil and felt before applying them was not immediately apparent, though the resulting jacket and overlapping seam made physical sense.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for more practical construction and discovery; the water system was straightforward but its physical details made it engaging.
